one-way-anova.formula: SSB = sum n_i (mean_i - grand)^2 (df = k-1); SSW = sum sum (x - mean_i)^2 (df = N-k); F = (SSB/(k-1)) / (SSW/(N-k)); upper-tail p = I(x; df_w/2, df_b/2) the regularized incomplete beta with x = df_w/(df_w + df_b F); eta^2 = SSB/(SSB+SSW).
one-way-anova.edition: Per OpenIntro Statistics Chapter 7 (comparing many means with ANOVA), by name; the F-distribution p-value reuses the bundled regularized-incomplete-beta helper. Verified against scipy.stats.f_oneway.
one-way-anova.freeAccess: Free at openintro.org; the F-test and its partition of variance are public-domain textbook statistics.
one-way-anova.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
one-way-anova.editionNote: One-way ANOVA generalizes the two-sample t-test to three or more groups. It partitions the total variation into a between-group part SSB = sum n_i (mean_i - grand)^2 on k-1 df and a within-group part SSW = sum (x - group mean)^2 on N-k df; the ratio of their mean squares F = (SSB/(k-1))/(SSW/(N-k)) is large when the group means are spread far apart relative to the scatter inside the groups. The p-value is the upper tail of the F distribution with those two df, computed from the bundled regularized incomplete beta. eta^2 = SSB/SST is the effect size (share of variance explained: ~0.01 small, 0.06 medium, 0.14 large). ANOVA assumes roughly normal groups with similar variances and reports only THAT at least one mean differs, not which - a post-hoc test such as Tukey HSD locates the difference. A statistics aid; the study design governs.

assumptions.name: Variance partition
assumptions.value: SST = SSB + SSW; F = MSB/MSW with df k-1 and N-k

assumptions.name: F-distribution p-value
assumptions.value: p = I(x; df_w/2, df_b/2) the regularized incomplete beta, x = df_w/(df_w+df_b F)

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: flags that a difference exists, not which pair (needs a Tukey HSD post-hoc); assumes normal groups, equal variances

digester-vs-loading.formula: VS_fed = feed_gal x 8.34 x (%TS/100) x (%VS/100); VSLR = VS_fed / volume x 1000; DT = volume x 7.48 / feed_gal.
digester-vs-loading.edition: Anaerobic digester volatile-solids loading rate (WEF; university operator courses), by name.
digester-vs-loading.freeAccess: The volatile-solids loading and detention-time relations are public wastewater-operations results; the digester monitoring and the operator govern.
digester-vs-loading.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
digester-vs-loading.editionNote: Overloading past about 400 lb VS/day per 1,000 ft^3 sours the digester as the acid-formers outrun the methane-formers and the pH and alkalinity crash (a slow failure that takes weeks to recover); the loading rate, not a full tank, is the health metric; a thin feed can hit the limit at high flow and a rich feed at low flow. The high-rate band is 100-400 lb VS/day per 1,000 ft^3. An operating aid, not a process design.

assumptions.name: High-rate band
assumptions.value: 100-400 lb VS/day per 1,000 ft^3; over ~400 the digester can sour

assumptions.name: Loading is the metric
assumptions.value: the loading rate, not a full tank, sets digester health; concentration and flow both matter

hp-from-torque.formula: HP = Torque(lb-ft) * RPM / 5252 (5252 = 33,000 / 2*pi); kW = HP * 0.7457. Torque and HP are equal at 5252 RPM by definition. Solve for any of {HP, torque, RPM}.
hp-from-torque.edition: Classical definition of mechanical power (Watt's 33,000 ft-lb/min); SAE J1349 engine-power rating, by name.
hp-from-torque.freeAccess: The constant 5252 is a pure derivation, fully public.
hp-from-torque.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
hp-from-torque.editionNote: Single-identity; brake/observed power per the inputs, not SAE-corrected unless the dyno applied the correction.

assumptions.name: Power constant
assumptions.value: 5252 = 33,000 ft-lb/min per HP / (2*pi rad/rev)

septic-drainfield-capacity.formula: Design flow supported = available_trench_ft × trench_width_ft × application_rate_gpd_per_ft² (the inverse of the required-area sizing). Bedrooms = floor(design_flow / gpd_per_bedroom); EPA baseline 150 gpd/bedroom.
septic-drainfield-capacity.edition: U.S. EPA Onsite Wastewater Treatment Systems Manual (EPA/625/R-00/008) by name; per-state and per-county application rates and per-bedroom design flows set by local code (not bundled).
septic-drainfield-capacity.freeAccess: Free at epa.gov/septic. State application-rate and per-bedroom-flow tables free on each state department of health / DEQ site.
septic-drainfield-capacity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
septic-drainfield-capacity.editionNote: Single-edition (EPA OWTS Manual + AHJ-supplied rates). The inverse of septic-drainfield: it answers how big a house a lot's field can serve. State and county codes set the application rate and the per-bedroom design flow (commonly 120-150 gpd); enter the values from your local code.

assumptions.name: Application rate
assumptions.value: user-supplied from local code (this tool deliberately does not bundle a per-state shard)

assumptions.name: Per-bedroom flow
assumptions.value: EPA baseline 150 gpd/bedroom; states vary (often 120)

manual-j-heating.formula: Heating load = U×A×ΔT for walls, ceiling and windows + U×A×0.5ΔT for the floor + infiltration sensible (1.08 × CFM_inf × ΔT). Simplified estimator only; ACCA Manual J 8th ed. is the code-compliant method.
manual-j-heating.edition: ACCA Manual J, 8th edition. NOAA NCEI heating design temperatures by location.
manual-j-heating.freeAccess: ACCA Manual J licensed. NOAA design temps free at ncei.noaa.gov.
manual-j-heating.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
manual-j-heating.editionNote: Editions available: ACCA Manual J 8th ed. is the current published edition. The simplified estimator on this tile is not a code-compliant load calculation; ACCA Manual J supersedes any rule of thumb the tile applies.

assumptions.name: Indoor design temperature
assumptions.value: 70 °F unless user supplies

assumptions.name: Outdoor design temperature
assumptions.value: user-entered (look up the NOAA NCEI 99% design value for the site)

assumptions.name: Air density factor
assumptions.value: 1.08 BTU/(hr × CFM × °F)

outdoor-air-mix.formula: Mixed dry bulb = f × T_OA + (1 − f) × T_RA; mixed humidity ratio mass-weighted the same way (f = OA fraction).
outdoor-air-mix.edition: ASHRAE 62.1-2022 (Ventilation for Acceptable Indoor Air Quality).
outdoor-air-mix.freeAccess: Free read-only access to ASHRAE standards at ashrae.org (Technical Resources, read-only standards).
outdoor-air-mix.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
outdoor-air-mix.editionNote: Editions available: ASHRAE 62.1-2022 is the current published edition; ASHRAE 62.1-2019 is widely adopted in jurisdictions on IECC 2018.

assumptions.name: OA fraction
assumptions.value: user-entered; ASHRAE 62.1 sets the minimum

joist-cantilever-check.formula: table_limit_ft = IRC 2021 Table R507.6 maximum cantilever for the joist size and species at the tabulated backspan column at or above backspan_ft (NP = not permitted); ratio_limit_ft = backspan_ft / 4; cantilever_max_ft = min(table_limit_ft, ratio_limit_ft); within_limit when overhang_ft <= cantilever_max_ft; margin_ft = cantilever_max_ft - overhang_ft.
joist-cantilever-check.edition: IRC 2021 Table R507.6 (deck joist spans and cantilevers, 40 psf live load), by name; backspan columns 4 to 18 ft. The AHJ-adopted IRC edition governs.
joist-cantilever-check.freeAccess: IRC Table R507.6 is a prescriptive table (many jurisdictions post the adopted IRC); the tile reads its cantilever columns for the entered joist size, species, and backspan.
joist-cantilever-check.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
joist-cantilever-check.editionNote: Deck-joist cantilever per IRC 2021 Table R507.6: the table lets a joist overhang by about a quarter of its backspan at short backspans, then caps the overhang or marks it NP (not permitted) by joist size and species as the backspan grows -- a Southern pine 2x10 on a 14 ft backspan may cantilever 3 ft 4 in, less than the 3 ft 6 in a bare 1:4 rule would allow. Between tabulated columns the tile reads the longer (more restrictive) column. A floor cantilever is a different check: R502.3.3 limits it to the nominal joist depth unless its own tables apply. Until 2026-09-25 this citation still described a bare backspan / 4 rule after the code had moved to the table.

assumptions.name: Table R507.6 cantilever
assumptions.value: maximum cantilever by joist size, species, and backspan column (4-18 ft), never more than backspan / 4; NP where the table forbids one

assumptions.name: Tip load is engineered
assumptions.value: a beam / wall / roof bearing on the cantilever tip is an engineered condition, not prescriptive

steam-kettle-heatup.formula: mass_lb = gallons x 8.34 x specific_gravity; heat_btu = mass_lb x specific_heat x (final_temp_f - start_temp_f); heatup_hr = heat_btu / (rated_input_btuh x jacket_efficiency); steam_per_batch_lb = heat_btu / (latent_heat_btu_lb x jacket_efficiency), the jacket condensing steam for the product and its losses; steam_rate_lb_hr = steam_per_batch_lb / heatup_hr; boiler_hp = steam_rate_lb_hr / 34.5.
steam-kettle-heatup.edition: The sensible-heat relation Q = m c dT with 8.34 lb per gallon of water, and steam demand from Q divided by the latent heat of saturated steam at the operating pressure and by the jacket efficiency (about 945.6 BTU/lb at 15 psig per the ASME steam tables), cited by name and not reproduced; boiler horsepower at 34.5 lb/hr of steam. The kettle's rated input and the boiler manufacturer's data govern.
steam-kettle-heatup.freeAccess: The sensible-heat relation and the boiler-horsepower definition are public. The kettle volume, product properties, temperatures, rated input, jacket efficiency, and steam latent heat are the user's values.
steam-kettle-heatup.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
steam-kettle-heatup.editionNote: A steam-jacketed kettle is a heat exchanger with a known duty, so the first half of the calculation is the ordinary sensible-heat relation and holds no surprises. The second half is the reason for the tile. Dividing the same heat requirement by the latent heat of the steam and by the jacket efficiency gives pounds of steam per batch, and dividing that by the heat-up time gives the pounds per hour the boiler must deliver during the come-up. Kettles are sized on batch volume and boilers on peak steam rate, and the peak is the come-up rather than the simmer, so a kitchen with four kettles that all start at six in the morning has a boiler problem that never appears on the equipment schedule. Staggering the starts halves the peak without changing a single piece of equipment. At 15 psig the latent heat of saturated steam is about 945.6 BTU/lb; higher pressure carries slightly less latent heat per pound but presents a larger temperature difference across the jacket, so it heats faster. The jacket efficiency accounts for the heat that does not reach the product. A sizing estimate; the kettle's rated input and the boiler manufacturer's data govern.

assumptions.name: Water density
assumptions.value: 8.34 lb per gallon, scaled by the product's specific gravity

assumptions.name: Latent heat of steam
assumptions.value: about 945.6 BTU/lb saturated at 15 psig; cited to the ASME steam tables, not reproduced

assumptions.name: Boiler horsepower
assumptions.value: 34.5 lb/hr of steam per boiler horsepower

assumptions.name: Peak is the come-up
assumptions.value: boilers are sized on the come-up steam rate, not the simmer

lab-safety-quickread.formula: Reference page; no compute. Two sections: GHS pictograms (name, signal word, hazards) and a four-step spill-response decision tree (assess / evacuate / contain / report).
lab-safety-quickread.edition: UN GHS Rev. 9 pictograms (cited by name only). OSHA Hazard Communication Standard 29 CFR 1910.1200 by section number only. EPA emergency-response framework cited by name.
lab-safety-quickread.governance: Math aid for personal verification. Stop work and consult the qualified person on site if any number does not match the field condition.
lab-safety-quickread.editionNote: Single-edition (reference). The hardened safety notice ('exceeds your lab's spill-kit capacity or unknown agent: stop, evacuate, call EH&S or 911') always appears.

mortgage-reserves.formula: required = PITI_monthly * reserves_months. eligible = liquid_assets + retirement_balance * retirement_allowable_pct/100. delta = eligible - required. months_covered = eligible / PITI_monthly.
mortgage-reserves.edition: Fannie Mae Single-Family Selling Guide B3-4.1-01 (reserves) and B3-4.3-03 (retirement-account funds). Freddie Mac Single-Family Seller/Servicer Guide 5501.2.
mortgage-reserves.freeAccess: Fannie Mae Selling Guide free at selling-guide.fanniemae.com; Freddie Mac Guide free at guide.freddiemac.com.
mortgage-reserves.governance: Estimate. Lender governs final underwriting and rate / fee disclosure. Appraiser governs the appraised value. State law and the agency's program guidelines may impose stricter limits than the published thresholds.
mortgage-reserves.editionNote: Required reserve months vary by loan type and program (conventional 0-6, jumbo 6-12, investment property 6+); the user enters the figure the lender requires. Fannie Mae B3-4.3-03 counts vested retirement funds for reserves with no percentage discount and without requiring withdrawal (the 100% default); where a program discounts retirement assets, enter its percentage. The allowable fraction and which assets count are lender- and program-specific.

assumptions.name: Reserve unit
assumptions.value: one month of full PITIA payment

assumptions.name: Retirement allowance
assumptions.value: default 100% of the vested balance (no discount in Fannie Mae B3-4.3-03), user-adjustable for a program that discounts

lighting-throw-for-pool.formula: throw = target_pool_diameter / (2 x tan(beam angle / 2)); the inverse of beam_diameter = 2 x throw x tan(beam angle / 2).
lighting-throw-for-pool.edition: First-principles theatrical photometry - the beam-spread geometry the form fixture photometric charts (manufacturer cut sheets) publish, solved for the throw, by name; public domain.
lighting-throw-for-pool.freeAccess: Public first-principles photometry. The beam / field angle comes from the fixture's photometric data.
lighting-throw-for-pool.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
lighting-throw-for-pool.editionNote: The throw distance a fixture needs to cast a target beam (pool) diameter, the inverse of lighting-beam: throw = D / (2 x tan(beam angle / 2)), in the entered unit. A wider beam angle reaches the same pool from a shorter throw. This is the geometry only; the center-beam illuminance still falls off with the square of the throw, so a farther hang for a larger pool is also a dimmer one (check the level with the lighting-beam tile). Enter the beam angle you are designing to (beam angle to 50% intensity, or the wider field angle to 10%). Single-edition (physics); the fixture cut sheet governs.

assumptions.name: Geometry only
assumptions.value: throw from beam spread; the illuminance still falls with the square of the throw (use lighting-beam for the level)

assumptions.name: Beam vs field angle
assumptions.value: enter the angle being designed to; beam angle is to 50% intensity, field angle to 10%

winch-fleet-angle.edition: Winch drum fleet angle (the Wire Rope Users Manual; ANSI E1.6 entertainment rigging), by name; the drum, rope, and equipment manufacturer govern.
winch-fleet-angle.freeAccess: The atan fleet-angle geometry is a published wire-rope-practice relation; the offset and lead come from the drum and sheave layout.
winch-fleet-angle.governance: Estimate. Head rigger and manufacturer working-load-limit charts govern. Inspect every piece of hardware before the show.
winch-fleet-angle.editionNote: Fleet angle is the sideways angle the wire rope makes as it runs from a fixed lead sheave onto the moving drum: fleet_angle = atan(lateral_offset / lead_distance). The lateral offset is the sideways distance from the sheave's groove plane to where the rope lands on the drum (largest at the drum ends); the lead distance is the perpendicular distance from drum to sheave; any consistent unit works because the ratio is dimensionless. The common guideline keeps the fleet angle at or below 1.5 deg for a grooved drum and 2 deg for a smooth drum; too large and the rope crushes earlier wraps or climbs the flange, too small (under about 0.5 deg) and it will not cross-wind and can pile up. Lengthening the lead or centering the sheave lowers the angle. A design guideline, not a rating; the drum, rope, and equipment manufacturer govern.

assumptions.name: Guideline limits
assumptions.value: at or below 1.5 deg grooved drum, 2 deg smooth drum; under ~0.5 deg risks pile-up
assumptions.source: Wire Rope Users Manual / ANSI E1.6

assumptions.name: Offset location
assumptions.value: the lateral offset is largest at the drum ends (sheave groove plane to rope landing)

sewage-loss-disposal.formula: in place = sum of (area x thickness / 12); loose = in place x bulking factor; bag cubic ft = bag gal / 7.48052; bags = ceil(loose / bag cubic ft); container cubic ft = cy x 27; utilisation = loose / container cubic ft; liquid weight = extracted gal x 8.3454.
sewage-loss-disposal.edition: In-place debris volume from area times thickness, a bulking factor applied to get the loose volume the container actually sees, bag count at 7.48052 gallons per cubic foot, and a container at 27 cubic ft per cubic yard, by name. The liquid fraction is reported separately because it routes separately. Whether Category 3 solids are ordinary construction debris or a regulated waste stream is a LOCAL determination. ANSI/IICRC S500, the local solid waste and sewer authorities, and OSHA govern.
sewage-loss-disposal.freeAccess: Volume arithmetic on the user's own demolition takeoff and an entered bulking factor; no waste classification or hauler table is reproduced.
sewage-loss-disposal.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
sewage-loss-disposal.editionNote: Demolition debris does not stay the size it was on the wall, and that is the error this calculation exists to prevent. Carpet and pad in particular bulk enormously once they are cut out and rolled, a factor of two to three being ordinary, so a takeoff done on in-place thickness underestimates the container by that factor -- which is why both volumes are printed and the container is sized on the loose one. The routing split is the part specific to a Category 3 loss, and it is the reason the liquid is reported separately rather than folded into the volume. Solids are bagged, sealed, and removed through the containment. Liquids are the extracted water, they are the larger number by weight on most losses, and they do not go in the box at all: they route to sanitary sewer where the authority permits it, which is a question to ask before the truck leaves rather than after. The common useful finding is that the roll-off ordered by habit is mostly empty, because the volume that looks enormous coming out of a house is small against a ten-yard box. What this does not do is weigh the debris, and weight rather than volume governs a haul on dense material -- the roll-off haul-count calculation handles that side and takes a debris volume as its input, so the two chain together. Bulking factors are observational and vary with the material and with how it is cut, rolled, or folded.

assumptions.name: Bulking is the whole point
assumptions.value: in-place thickness underestimates the container by the bulking factor; size on the loose volume

assumptions.name: Liquid routes separately
assumptions.value: extracted water is the larger number by weight and does not go in the box

assumptions.name: Solids classification is local
assumptions.value: jurisdictions differ on whether Category 3 solids are ordinary construction debris

awning-canopy-load.formula: area = projection x width; q = 0.00256 x V^2 x Kz x Kzt x Kd; uplift pressure = q x Cn uplift and downward = q x Cn downward; force = pressure x area; pf = 0.7 x Ce x Ct x pg (ASCE 7-22, no Is); snow force = pf x area; net uplift = uplift force - dead load x area.
awning-canopy-load.edition: Velocity pressure q = 0.00256 x V^2 x Kz x Kzt x Kd and the ATTACHED-CANOPY net pressure coefficients of ASCE 7 Chapter 29, cited by chapter and linked, with no ASCE table reproduced -- Cn is entered by the user. Flat-roof snow from ASCE 7-22 Chapter 7, pf = 0.7 x Ce x Ct x pg (Eq. 7.3-1, no Is), cited by chapter. Load only, not a canopy design. ASCE 7, the structural engineer, and the AHJ govern.
awning-canopy-load.freeAccess: The velocity-pressure and flat-roof snow relations are stated and cited to their chapters; every coefficient is a user-entered value from the applicable ASCE 7 provisions rather than a reproduced table.
awning-canopy-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
awning-canopy-load.editionNote: A canopy is open underneath, so wind acts on both faces at once -- pressure on top and suction below, or the reverse -- and ASCE 7 handles that with a net pressure coefficient rather than the separate external and internal coefficients used on an enclosed building. That single difference is what separates a canopy from a roof. On a roof, gravity is the design case and wind uplift is a check; on a canopy the uplift case frequently governs outright, and it loads the wall anchors in tension and the connection in prying, which are the two load directions masonry and stud walls are worst at and the two that get detailed most casually because the canopy looks light. Both cases have to be run because they come from different weather: the snow case governs the members and the deflection, the uplift case governs the anchors. The canopy's own dead weight offsets only a small fraction of the uplift, which is the arithmetic that decides between through-bolting with backing plates and lagging into a stud. This is load only. It sizes no member, connection, or anchor, computes no prying or eccentric moment at the wall, and checks no wall or backup for the tension it is being asked to carry, which on masonry is frequently the actual limit.

assumptions.name: Net coefficient, both faces
assumptions.value: an open canopy uses a NET Cn rather than separate external and internal coefficients

assumptions.name: Uplift usually governs
assumptions.value: and it loads the wall anchors in tension and the connection in prying

assumptions.name: Drift not modeled
assumptions.value: sliding and drifting snow off the roof above can far exceed the flat-roof value

pool-interior-finish-volume.formula: interior_area_sf = length_ft x width_ft + 2 x (length_ft + width_ft) x avg_depth_ft; gunite_cy = interior_area_sf x (shell_thickness_in/12) / 27 x (1 + waste_pct/100); plaster_cy = interior_area_sf x (plaster_thickness_in/12) / 27.
pool-interior-finish-volume.edition: Pool interior-finish identity by name (interior from floor plus walls; gunite and plaster volumes over the interior area); first-principles arithmetic.
pool-interior-finish-volume.freeAccess: The volume arithmetic is public first-principles; the shell and plaster thicknesses come from the spec.
pool-interior-finish-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pool-interior-finish-volume.editionNote: The shell (gunite or shotcrete) and plaster thicknesses come from the spec. Gunite rebound is on top of the neat volume (see shotcrete-rebound-quantity). The average depth is the volumetric average of the shallow and deep ends. Distinct from the water pool-volume.

assumptions.name: Interior area
assumptions.value: floor (L x W) plus walls (2 x (L + W) x avg depth) for a rectangular pool

assumptions.name: Shell / plaster
assumptions.value: ~8 in gunite shell and ~3/8 in plaster (defaults); the spec governs

suspended-ceiling-grid.formula: area_sf = room_length_ft x room_width_ft; panels = ceil(area_sf/8); main_tee_lf = area_sf/4; cross_tee_lf = area_sf/2; wall_angle_lf = 2 x (room_length_ft + room_width_ft); hangers = ceil(area_sf/16).
suspended-ceiling-grid.edition: Suspended-ceiling 2x4 grid takeoff ratios by name (panels, tees, wall angle, and hangers from the area and perimeter); first-principles geometry.
suspended-ceiling-grid.freeAccess: The grid takeoff ratios are public quantity geometry; the reflected ceiling plan and seismic bracing come from the plans and code.
suspended-ceiling-grid.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
suspended-ceiling-grid.editionNote: The ratios are for a standard 2x4 lay-in grid. A 2x2 grid adds the 2-ft cross tees (adding half again to the cross-tee run). Hangers are on the mains at 4 ft on center. Seismic areas add bracing and clips per code; the reflected ceiling plan governs the layout.

assumptions.name: Grid
assumptions.value: standard 2x4 lay-in (8 sf panel); a 2x2 grid adds half again to the cross-tee run

assumptions.name: Hangers
assumptions.value: on the mains at 4 ft on center; seismic areas add bracing and clips per code

firewood-cord.formula: cords = length_ft x height_ft x depth_ft / 128; a full (standard) cord = 128 stacked cubic feet.
firewood-cord.edition: NIST Handbook 130, Uniform Regulation for the Method of Sale of Commodities (firewood sold by the cord = 128 ft^3).
firewood-cord.freeAccess: NIST Handbook 130 is free at nist.gov.
firewood-cord.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
firewood-cord.editionNote: A full (standard) cord is 128 stacked cubic feet - a 4 ft x 4 ft x 8 ft rick of tightly stacked wood - so cords = length x height x depth (the log length) / 128. Under NIST Handbook 130 firewood must be advertised and sold by the cord or a fraction of a cord; 'face cord', 'rick', 'rack', and 'truckload' are not legal units of measure because they depend on the (unstated) log length. The 128 ft^3 is STACKED volume including the air gaps between pieces, so the solid wood content is roughly 70-90% depending on how straight and tightly stacked the pieces are; loosely thrown wood occupies more space than the same wood stacked. A measurement aid; the point-of-sale regulation and the state weights-and-measures office govern the legal sale.

assumptions.name: Full cord
assumptions.value: 128 stacked cubic feet (4 x 4 x 8 ft)

assumptions.name: Legal unit
assumptions.value: the cord or a fraction of a cord; 'face cord' / 'rick' are not legal units

assumptions.name: Stacked volume
assumptions.value: includes air gaps; solid wood is ~70-90% of the stacked volume

bolt-circle.formula: R = dia/2; hole i at angle start + i*(360/N): x = cx + R*cos(angle), y = cy + R*sin(angle); angular spacing = 360/N; adjacent center-to-center chord = 2*R*sin(180/N).
bolt-circle.edition: Circle-of-holes (bolt-circle) layout - the standard hole-pattern coordinate geometry as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; first-principles trigonometry.
bolt-circle.freeAccess: Pure trigonometry, public; confirm the hole pattern, datum, and tolerance against the drawing before drilling.
bolt-circle.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bolt-circle.editionNote: First-principles circle geometry; holes run counter-clockwise from the start angle (measured from +X). The drawing's datum and tolerance govern.

assumptions.name: Even spacing
assumptions.value: the N holes are evenly spaced on one circle; for an unequal pattern enter each radius/angle directly

bend-springback.formula: x = tool_radius x yield_strength / (modulus x thickness); springback factor Ks = Ri/Rf = 4 x^3 - 3 x + 1; released (final) radius Rf = tool_radius / Ks. E ~ 29-30e6 psi steel, ~10e6 aluminum.
bend-springback.edition: Sheet-metal bend-springback relation (Machinery's Handbook / ASM Metals Handbook forming), by name; the material certificate, the tooling method, and a test bend govern the actual overbend.
bend-springback.freeAccess: The springback cubic is a published forming relation; the tool radius, thickness, yield strength, and modulus come from the setup and the material certificate.
bend-springback.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bend-springback.editionNote: When a bent sheet is released from the die, the elastic part of the strain recovers and the bend springs OPEN -- the radius increases and the included angle grows. The Machinery's Handbook (and ASM Metals Handbook) springback relation expresses this as a springback factor Ks = Ri/Rf = 4 x^3 - 3 x + 1, where x = Ri x yield strength / (E x thickness) is a dimensionless measure of how much elastic strain the bend stores: Ri is the inside (tool) radius, E the elastic modulus (about 29-30 million psi for steel, 10 million for aluminum), and the yield strength and thickness from the material. Because Ks is slightly less than 1, the released radius Rf = Ri / Ks is larger than the radius held in the tooling, so the operator must OVERBEND -- form to a tighter radius and a smaller angle than the target so the part relaxes onto it. A 1-inch tool radius in 0.1-inch, 50-ksi steel gives Ks = 0.948, so the radius springs from 1.00 to 1.05 inches, about 5%; a higher-yield or aluminum part (a larger yield/E ratio) springs back more, and a thicker part less. This radius relation captures the elastic recovery, but the exact overbend a shop dials in also depends strongly on the tooling method -- air bending springs back the most, bottoming less, and coining (which plastically sets the radius under high tonnage) nearly eliminates springback -- as well as the grain direction and the press, so the first article is always checked with a protractor and radius gauge and the setup trimmed. A screen; the material certificate, the tooling method, and a test bend govern the actual overbend.

assumptions.name: Springback cubic
assumptions.value: Ks = Ri/Rf = 4 x^3 - 3 x + 1, x = Ri x yield / (E x thickness); released radius Rf = Ri/Ks > Ri (overbend needed)

assumptions.name: Tooling-dependent
assumptions.value: air bend springs most, bottoming less, coining nearly none; grain direction and press also matter; a test bend sets the final overbend

projector-max-screen-size.formula: Max screen area = lumens x gain / target foot-lamberts; width = sqrt(area x aspect_w / aspect_h), height = width x aspect_h / aspect_w, diagonal = sqrt(width^2 + height^2).
projector-max-screen-size.edition: Standard AV screen-luminance identity (SMPTE-style targets, by name); foot-lamberts = lumens x gain / area, solved for the area.
projector-max-screen-size.freeAccess: Screen-luminance methods free at projector and screen maker technical pages.
projector-max-screen-size.governance: Math aid for personal verification. Stop work and consult the qualified person on site if any number does not match the field condition.
projector-max-screen-size.editionNote: Single-edition (engineering-practice / first-principles take-off; refresh as practice and product data shift).

assumptions.name: Target luminance band
assumptions.value: ~16 fL dark room, ~30-50 fL ambient (default 16, editable)

pull-box-sizing.formula: Straight pull: min = 8 x largest raceway. Angle/U pull: min = 6 x largest raceway + sum of same-row others. Between same-conductor entries: >= 6 x larger raceway.
pull-box-sizing.freeAccess: NFPA 70 free read-only at nfpa.org (registration); the multipliers are stated, not reproduced.
pull-box-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pull-box-sizing.editionNote: Single-edition (the code section and the design standard govern; the AHJ is the law).

assumptions.name: Straight-pull multiplier
assumptions.value: 8x the largest raceway trade size (NEC 314.28(A)(1))

assumptions.name: Angle/U-pull multiplier
assumptions.value: 6x the largest raceway + the sum of the other same-row raceways (NEC 314.28(A)(2))

assumptions.name: Minimums only
assumptions.value: the box's listed dimensions, conductor bending space, and the AHJ govern

governor-tripping-speed.formula: minimum mechanical trip = rated speed x the code minimum percentage, commonly 115; margin = (trip - rated) / rated; the electrical overspeed switch must open at not more than 90% of the mechanical trip above 150 fpm up to 500 fpm (and with static control), 95% above 500 fpm, 100% at 150 fpm or less or with a speed-reducing switch (A17.1 2.18.4.1.2; California Title 8 3036(d)(4)); buffer impact speed = the mechanical trip.
governor-tripping-speed.edition: The ASME A17.1 governor tripping-speed limits by name -- a mechanical trip at least 115% of rated speed under a ceiling that tightens as rated speed rises, with the electrical switch opening at not more than 90% or 95% of it by rated speed (A17.1 2.18.4.1.2). Both trip bounds are entered from the adopted code table, not reproduced; the switch percentages are shipped.
governor-tripping-speed.freeAccess: Percentage comparison against code values the user supplies; no A17.1 table is reproduced.
governor-tripping-speed.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
governor-tripping-speed.editionNote: Two devices operate at two speeds and the order matters. The electrical overspeed switch trips first, cutting power and setting the brake, which stops most overspeed events without the safety ever engaging. Only if the car continues to accelerate does the governor mechanically grip its rope and pull the safety, which wedges the car against the guide rails -- a violent event that takes the car out of service and requires inspection afterward. A governor with the two settings inverted, or with the electrical trip inoperative, removes the gentle stop and leaves only the violent one. The margin band is bounded at both ends for good reasons. The minimum ensures the governor does not trip on normal operation, including the modest overspeed that occurs on a heavily loaded down run. The maximum exists because a safety must engage before the car reaches a speed at which the buffers below it cannot absorb the impact, so governor trip, safety type, and buffer stroke are a set rather than independent choices. The governor rope runs at car speed regardless of the suspension roping, which is worth stating because a mechanic used to thinking in 2 to 1 terms can misread what the governor is seeing. Verification is by test at the intervals the code requires: a governor is a mechanical device with springs and pivots that age, and a setting recorded on a tag is not evidence of a setting that still holds.

assumptions.name: The electrical trip must come first, with room
assumptions.value: not more than 90% of the trip to 500 fpm (and static control), 95% above; 100% only with a speed-reducing switch

assumptions.name: Trip, safety and buffer are one set
assumptions.value: raising the trip invalidates the buffer selection beneath it

assumptions.name: A tag is not evidence
assumptions.value: tripping speed is verified by test at the intervals the code requires

revolving-door-throughput.formula: theoretical people per hour = rotations per minute x wings x people per compartment x 60, discounted by a utilization factor; peak rate = population x peak fraction / the peak window in hours; doors required = the peak rate divided by the discounted throughput, rounded up.
revolving-door-throughput.edition: The compartment throughput relation by name, compared against a peak arrival rate rather than a daily average, with the adopted building and fire codes named as governing the egress credit a revolving door or turnstile receives.
revolving-door-throughput.freeAccess: Rate arithmetic on figures the user supplies; no manufacturer capacity table is reproduced.
revolving-door-throughput.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
revolving-door-throughput.editionNote: The headline throughput and the achievable one differ, and the difference is behaviour: people arrive unevenly, carry things, hesitate, and do not fill every compartment, so a realistic figure is a large discount on the theoretical one and designing to the theoretical number produces a queue at the one moment the building is judged on it. The comparison that matters is against the PEAK. A building of two thousand people does not arrive over eight hours; it arrives in two twenty-minute waves, and the design case is that wave. Dividing daily population by operating hours produces a number that flatters every entrance ever built, and the two are printed side by side here because they routinely differ by a factor of ten or more (4,200 against 250 people an hour in the example). Egress is a separate and code-governed matter. Revolving doors and turnstiles receive limited or no credit toward required egress capacity depending on the code and the arrangement, so a lobby that meets its throughput target with revolving doors alone still needs conventional swinging doors for egress, and the two requirements are sized independently. The utilization discount is a judgment rather than a measurement, and bidirectional use roughly halves a revolving door's one-way figure.

assumptions.name: Design to the peak, not the average
assumptions.value: they routinely differ by a factor of ten or more (4,200 against 250 people an hour in the example), and the building is judged at the peak

assumptions.name: Utilization is a judgment
assumptions.value: bag and cart traffic, badge interaction, and bidirectional use all cut the theoretical figure

assumptions.name: Egress is sized separately
assumptions.value: revolving doors and turnstiles carry limited or no egress credit

cipp-fully-deteriorated.formula: ASTM F1216 Appendix X1, fully deteriorated gravity pipe: thickness = the greatest of X1.3 t = [0.375 (N q_t / C) squared D cubed / (E_L R_w B' E's)]^(1/3) with q_t = 0.433 H_w + w H_s R_w / 144 + W_s, R_w = 1 - 0.33 H_w / H_s (not under 0.67), B' = 1 / (1 + 4 e^(-0.065 H_s)); X1.4 t = D (1.116 / E)^(1/3) (E I / D cubed at least 0.093 on the initial modulus); X1.1 groundwater buckling; X1.2 ovality bending against the long-term flexural strength. C = ((1 - q) / (1 + q) squared) cubed.
cipp-fully-deteriorated.edition: ASTM F1216 Appendix X1 design relations by name, worked as in the Iowa SUDAS Design Manual Section 14C-2 (Equations 14C-2.02 to 14C-2.11 and the fully deteriorated design example).
cipp-fully-deteriorated.freeAccess: The Iowa SUDAS Design Manual Section 14C-2 is free at iowasudas.org; ASTM F1216 itself is licensed and no table from it is reproduced.
cipp-fully-deteriorated.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
cipp-fully-deteriorated.editionNote: Checked against the SUDAS fully deteriorated example: a 12 in VCP under 5 ft of clay at 120 pcf, 2 ft of groundwater, HS-20 traffic (2 psi), 5% ovality, E's 1,000 psi, E 300,000 / E_L 150,000 psi. The manual gives 0.199 in from X1.3 (this computes 0.1996 with B' unrounded) against 0.186 in for stiffness. The manual's bending check carries 0.4 psi of water where its own Step 1 computes 0.87 psi; this uses the 0.87.

assumptions.name: Soil modulus E's
assumptions.value: 500 psi for badly cracked pipe with voids to 2,000 psi for fair pipe

co-alarm-placement.formula: required when a fuel-fired appliance is installed in the dwelling OR the dwelling has an attached garage; alarms = one outside each separate sleeping area, plus one inside each bedroom containing a fuel-burning appliance in the bedroom or its attached bathroom, plus (only where a local amendment adds it) one per story beyond the first.
co-alarm-placement.edition: IRC R315.2 (where required, for new construction: outside each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms, in dwelling units within which fuel-fired appliances are installed and in dwelling units that have attached garages) and IRC R315.3 (location, with the exception placing an alarm within a bedroom where a fuel-burning appliance is located in that bedroom or its attached bathroom).
co-alarm-placement.freeAccess: Both provisions are short prescriptive sentences reproduced in state adoptions and building-department bulletins. No table is reproduced.
co-alarm-placement.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
co-alarm-placement.editionNote: The value of this tile is the contrast with smoke alarms, because the two get conflated in both directions. First, CO alarms are a function of a SOURCE, not of the dwelling existing: R315.2 triggers on a fuel-fired appliance installed in the dwelling or on an attached garage. An all-electric house with a detached garage legitimately needs none, and the attached-garage trigger is the one people miss - a house with no gas at all still needs alarms if the garage is attached, because the source is a car. Second, and this is where money gets wasted, the required alarm goes OUTSIDE each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms, NOT in each bedroom. Applying the smoke-alarm count to CO is how a three-bedroom house ends up with five CO alarms when the code asks for one. The single case that does put an alarm inside a bedroom is R315.3's exception: a fuel-burning appliance located within that bedroom or its attached bathroom. A per-story requirement is deliberately NOT applied by default - the model IRC has no per-story rule for CO the way it does for smoke - but many states and cities amend one in, so it is an explicit toggle the user turns on rather than a hidden assumption either way. One placement detail the count cannot capture: immediate vicinity of the bedrooms means the corridor or space serving them, so a single alarm can cover several bedrooms off one hall while bedrooms at opposite ends of a house are separate sleeping AREAS and each need their own - count areas, not doors. Not checked: combination smoke/CO alarms and how they satisfy both sections at once, interconnection, primary power and battery backup and the battery-only allowances in existing construction, the alteration and addition triggers that pull existing dwellings in, detector-and-panel systems used in place of alarms, mounting height (usually governed by the listing rather than the code), and state amendments generally, which are more common and more varied on CO than on smoke. A screen; the adopted code, the alarm's listing, and the AHJ govern.

assumptions.name: Trigger
assumptions.value: a fuel-fired appliance in the dwelling OR an attached garage

assumptions.name: Base count
assumptions.value: one outside each separate sleeping area - NOT one per bedroom

assumptions.name: Bedroom exception
assumptions.value: one inside a bedroom with a fuel-burning appliance in it or its attached bathroom

assumptions.name: Per story
assumptions.value: NOT in the model IRC; an explicit opt-in toggle for local amendments

assumptions.name: Sleeping areas, not doors
assumptions.value: one alarm can serve several bedrooms off one hall

assumptions.name: Not checked
assumptions.value: combination alarms, interconnection, power, existing-dwelling triggers, panels, mounting height

crane-outrigger-reaction.formula: even = (W + Wc)/4; overturning M = W x R - Wc x Rc; R_max = even + M/(sqrt(2) x spread).
crane-outrigger-reaction.edition: Crane load-moment method / SAE J1063 stability, by name.
crane-outrigger-reaction.freeAccess: The over-corner outrigger-reaction estimate is a public statics result; the crane manufacturer's load-moment chart governs.
crane-outrigger-reaction.governance: Estimate. Head rigger and manufacturer working-load-limit charts govern. Inspect every piece of hardware before the show.
crane-outrigger-reaction.editionNote: The maximum reaction is not a quarter of the total because swinging the boom over a corner concentrates the overturning into one diagonal outrigger (which can carry well over half the load); a wider outrigger spread lowers the reaction; this is a planning estimate that feeds crane-ground-bearing. A planning estimate, not the crane rating.

assumptions.name: Over-corner concentration
assumptions.value: R_max = (W+Wc)/4 + M/(sqrt(2) x spread); the diagonal outrigger takes the overturning

assumptions.name: Chart governs
assumptions.value: the crane manufacturer's load-moment chart and published outrigger reaction data are authoritative

annular-grout-volume.formula: annular_area_in2 = (pi/4) x (bore_dia_in^2 - carrier_od_in^2); neat_ft3 = annular_area_in2 / 144 x length_ft; grout_cy = neat_ft3 / 27 x (1 + waste_pct/100); grout_gal = neat_ft3 x 7.48052 x (1 + waste_pct/100).
annular-grout-volume.edition: Annular-area identity by name (ring between two concentric circles); first-principles volume arithmetic.
annular-grout-volume.freeAccess: The annular-area identity is public geometry; the 7.48052 gal/ft^3 constant is exact.
annular-grout-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
annular-grout-volume.editionNote: The grout fills the void so the carrier neither floats during the pour nor settles after. The theoretical volume assumes a clean concentric annulus; the field always overruns it (voids, overcut, an out-of-round bore), so the waste factor is a floor, not a ceiling. The mix design and the AHJ / owner spec govern.

assumptions.name: Waste factor
assumptions.value: 5% pumping / overcut default; the field always overruns the neat annulus

assumptions.name: Volume constants
assumptions.value: 144 in^2/ft^2, 27 ft^3/cy, 7.48052 gal/ft^3 (exact)

thermal-stress-max-deltat.formula: dT_max = allowable_stress_psi / (E x alpha x restraint); the inverse of sigma = E alpha dT x restraint.
thermal-stress-max-deltat.edition: The standard restrained thermal-stress relation (mechanics of materials) solved for the temperature change, by name.
thermal-stress-max-deltat.freeAccess: The restrained thermal-stress relation is published free in any mechanics-of-materials reference. The engineer of record governs the design.
thermal-stress-max-deltat.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
thermal-stress-max-deltat.editionNote: The largest temperature change a restrained member can take before its thermal stress reaches the allowable, the inverse of thermal-stress-restrained: dT_max = sigma_allow / (E x alpha x restraint). The stress is independent of length, so the limit depends only on the material (modulus E, expansion coefficient alpha), the restraint factor, and the allowable stress. Heating a restrained member is compression and cooling is tension; if the allowable differs by direction, use the governing (smaller) one. A lower modulus or expansion coefficient, or partial restraint, raises the tolerable swing, which is why aluminum can take a larger temperature change than steel for the same stress. Fully restrained (factor 1) is the worst case; it does not check member buckling under the induced compression. A design aid, not a substitute for the engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Restrained-stress inverse
assumptions.value: dT_max = sigma_allow / (E alpha restraint), independent of length

assumptions.name: Sign
assumptions.value: heating a restrained member -> compression; cooling -> tension; use the governing allowable

assumptions.name: No buckling check
assumptions.value: fully restrained is the worst case; buckling under the compression is not checked

tr55-time-of-concentration.formula: Tc = Tt_sheet + Tt_shallow + Tt_channel. Sheet (TR-55 Eq 3-3): Tt = 0.007 (n L)^0.8 / (P2^0.5 s^0.4) hr. Shallow concentrated: V = 16.1345 sqrt(s) unpaved / 20.3282 sqrt(s) paved, Tt = L/(3600 V) hr. Channel (Manning): V = (1.49/n) R^(2/3) sqrt(s), Tt = L/(3600 V) hr.
tr55-time-of-concentration.edition: The NRCS TR-55 (Urban Hydrology for Small Watersheds, 1986) Chapter 3 velocity method for time of concentration, by name; constants verified against the TR-55 Chapter 3 worked example.
tr55-time-of-concentration.freeAccess: TR-55 is a free USDA NRCS publication; the sheet/shallow/channel travel-time equations and their constants are published in it and in every hydrology text.
tr55-time-of-concentration.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
tr55-time-of-concentration.editionNote: The TR-55 velocity method sums the travel time through up to three flow regimes to the time of concentration. SHEET flow (the plane at the head of the watershed, capped at 100 ft in the 2010 revision) uses Tt = 0.007 (n L)^0.8 / (P2^0.5 s^0.4) with n the overland roughness (about 0.011 smooth paved, 0.15 short grass, 0.24 dense grass, 0.40 light woods) and P2 the local 2-year 24-hour rainfall. SHALLOW CONCENTRATED flow in rills and swales uses V = 16.13 sqrt(s) unpaved or 20.33 sqrt(s) paved. CHANNEL flow uses Manning V = (1.49/n) R^(2/3) sqrt(s). Enter a length of 0 to skip a segment. This is the three-segment method the Kirpich time-of-concentration tile approximates in one channel equation. The overland roughness and the 2-year rainfall are user-supplied; a low d/D or a bad n shifts the answer. A design aid, not a substitute for a licensed civil engineer's drainage report; the engineer of record and the local drainage manual govern.

assumptions.name: Shallow concentrated
assumptions.value: V = 16.1345 sqrt(s) unpaved / 20.3282 sqrt(s) paved

assumptions.name: Channel
assumptions.value: Manning V = (1.49/n) R^(2/3) sqrt(s), Tt = L / (3600 V)

assumptions.name: Use
assumptions.value: Tc sets the design storm duration read off the local IDF curve, not a routed hydrograph

concrete-bearing-strength.formula: sqrt_ratio = min(sqrt(A2 / A1), 2.0); Bn = 0.85 f'c A1 sqrt_ratio; phi Bn = 0.65 Bn; DCR = Pu / phi Bn.
concrete-bearing-strength.edition: The ACI 318-19 22.8.3 bearing strength of concrete, with the 22.8.3.2 confinement multiplier sqrt(A2/A1) capped at 2.0 and phi = 0.65 for bearing (21.2), by name.
concrete-bearing-strength.freeAccess: ACI 318 is readable free through the ACI online reading room at concrete.org; the 22.8 bearing provisions are in the published code.
concrete-bearing-strength.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
concrete-bearing-strength.editionNote: The ACI 318-19 22.8.3 bearing strength Bn = 0.85 f'c A1 times the confinement factor sqrt(A2/A1), phi Bn = 0.65 Bn, and DCR = Pu / phi Bn. The sqrt(A2/A1) bonus applies only when the supporting surface is wider than the loaded area on all sides and the slopes/steps meet 22.8.3.2, and it is capped at 2.0. phi = 0.65 for bearing (21.2). A required bearing area exceeding the member may need a bearing plate or confinement reinforcement. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural engineer of record's stamped design.

assumptions.name: Nominal strength
assumptions.value: Bn = 0.85 f'c on the loaded area A1

assumptions.name: Confinement bonus
assumptions.value: multiply by sqrt(A2/A1) when the support is wider on all sides, capped at 2.0

assumptions.name: Strength reduction
assumptions.value: phi = 0.65 for bearing

formwork-member-spacing.formula: w = pressure x tributary / 144; bending L = sqrt(10 Fb S / w); shear L = (2/3 Fv b d)/(0.6 w); deflection L = cbrt(145 E I/(w x denominator)); the smallest governs.
formwork-member-spacing.edition: Formwork members analyzed as continuous beams over three or more equal spans, the standard ACI 347 formwork-design approach, by name.
formwork-member-spacing.freeAccess: The continuous-beam results are public structural mechanics; ACI 347 is available through ACI and its approach is reproduced in free formwork design guides.
formwork-member-spacing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
formwork-member-spacing.editionNote: The three coefficients are EXACT continuous-beam results for three or more equal spans, not formwork fudge factors: the interior-support moment is w L^2/10, the reaction there is 0.6 w L, and the end-span deflection is 0.0069 w L^4/EI, whose reciprocal is the familiar 145. SHEAR usually governs short, deep formwork members - the pinned 2x4 allows 24.7 in by bending and 41.0 by deflection but only 21.0 by shear - so sizing by bending alone over-spans the form. Use DRESSED dimensions (a 2x4 is 1.5 x 3.5) and allowable stresses already adjusted for the short load duration formwork enjoys; unadjusted table values under-report the spacing. The load is the form pressure times the tributary width: for studs that is the sheathing span, for wales the stud spacing. Two or fewer spans are a different case with higher moments. Bearing at supports, lateral bracing, and the ties are separate checks. ACI 347 and the engineer of record govern - a formwork failure is a collapse, not a redo.

assumptions.name: Three or more spans
assumptions.value: continuous-beam coefficients wL^2/10, 0.6wL, and wL^4/145EI apply to that case only

assumptions.name: Dressed and adjusted
assumptions.value: dimensions dressed, Fb and Fv already adjusted for short load duration
assumptions.source: user input, stated in the field labels

assumptions.name: Shear governs short members
assumptions.value: the check most often skipped and most often controlling

steel-doubler-plate.formula: phiRn_bare = 0.90 x 0.60 Fy dc tw; t_strength = max(0, Vu - phiRn_bare) / (0.90 x 0.60 Fy dc); t_stability = (dz + wz)/90 (the AISC 341 Seismic Provisions panel-zone limit; not in AISC 360, whose Eq. J10-12 is the high-axial panel-zone strength); t_required = max(t_strength, t_stability) when a doubler is needed.
steel-doubler-plate.edition: The AISC 360-16 Section J10.6 panel-zone doubler-plate strength, Eq. J10-9, with the (dz + wz)/90 stability limit from the AISC 341 Seismic Provisions, by name.
steel-doubler-plate.freeAccess: AISC 360 is available through AISC; the J10.6 panel-zone and doubler-plate provisions are published design equations.
steel-doubler-plate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
steel-doubler-plate.editionNote: The (dz + wz)/90 stability minimum (AISC 341) applies per individual doubler plate when it is not plug-welded to the web; a plug-welded doubler lets the combined thickness resist buckling. The basic bare strength (J10-9) is used for the shortfall - the flange-stiffened bonus (J10-11) is only allowed when panel-zone deformation is modeled. A high column axial load (Pr > 0.4 Pc) reduces the strength further and is not applied. Above roughly a half-inch shortfall the engineer often chooses a heavier column or a pair of plates. AISC 360 and the engineer of record govern - a detailing aid, not a stamped connection design.

assumptions.name: Two limits
assumptions.value: the doubler is the greater of the strength thickness (shortfall / 0.90 x 0.60 Fy dc) and the stability minimum (dz + wz)/90

assumptions.name: Not plug-welded
assumptions.value: the (dz + wz)/90 limit governs per plate unless the doubler is plug-welded to the web, when the combined thickness resists buckling

bound-water.formula: dry_mass_lb = material_volume_ft3 x dry_density_lb_ft3; water_lb = dry_mass_lb x (mc_current_pct - mc_goal_pct) / 100; water_gal = water_lb / 8.34 lb/gal.
bound-water.edition: Gravimetric water-mass relation, by name; ANSI/IICRC S500. Moisture content on a dry-weight basis (consistent with wood-emc). The 8.34 lb/gal water density is not edition-bound.
bound-water.freeAccess: Quantifies the pounds and gallons the drying system must evaporate from wet materials, scoping equipment-days against the dry goal.
bound-water.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bound-water.editionNote: Single-edition (the gravimetric relation does not roll). Moisture content is dry-weight basis; dry density and material moisture vary by species and product. This is a PLANNING estimate, not a gravimetric measurement - in-situ meter readings and the restorer's judgment GOVERN. ANSI/IICRC S500 names the dry standard.

assumptions.name: Dry-weight basis
assumptions.value: moisture content is percent of oven-dry weight, consistent with wood-emc

assumptions.name: Water density
assumptions.value: 8.34 lb/gal

rt-exposure-time.formula: exposure scales with the INVERSE SQUARE of source-to-film distance, t2 = t1 x (d2/d1)^2; geometric unsharpness Ug = source size x material thickness / (source-to-film distance - thickness), the source-to-object distance of ASME V T-274, falls only in direct proportion; and source activity decays as 0.5^(days / half-life), Ir-192 at 73.83 days and Co-60 at 1,925.3 days.
rt-exposure-time.edition: Radiographic technique arithmetic. The unsharpness LIMIT comes from the applicable code section for the thickness and is entered, as is the half-life so both common industrial sources are covered.
rt-exposure-time.freeAccess: One inverse-square relation, one geometric ratio, and one exponential decay.
rt-exposure-time.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
rt-exposure-time.editionNote: The trade is always the same shape: unsharpness improves linearly with distance and exposure worsens quadratically, so whether the longer shot is worth buying depends entirely on the code's unsharpness limit for the thickness. If the short distance already passes, the extra distance buys nothing the code asks for; if it fails, the minimum distance that meets it is the number wanted. SOURCE DECAY IS THE ERROR THAT NEEDS NOTHING TO GO WRONG -- an Ir-192 source loses half its activity in about 74 days, so a technique sheet written two months ago and used unchanged underexposes by nearly half, and the result is a light radiograph that may be interpreted rather than rejected.

assumptions.name: Unsharpness limit is entered
assumptions.value: it varies with thickness and code section

assumptions.name: Not a radiation safety calculation
assumptions.value: the restricted-area boundary is a separate question
assumptions.source: 10 CFR Part 34 or the state equivalent

saturated-steam-properties.formula: Absolute pressure = gauge + atmosphere. Saturation temperature from IAPWS-IF97 Eq. 31. Saturated liquid volume and enthalpy (vf, hf) from the region 1 Gibbs equation, Eq. 7, and saturated vapor (vg, hg) from the region 2 Gibbs equation, Eq. 15, both evaluated at the saturation temperature and pressure: v = (R T / p) pi gamma_pi, h = R T tau gamma_tau, R = 0.461526 kJ/(kg K). hfg = hg - hf. Converted with 1 psi = 6,894.757 Pa, 1 Btu/lb = 2.326 kJ/kg, 1 cu ft/lb = 0.0624280 m3/kg.
saturated-steam-properties.edition: IAPWS R7-97(2012), Revised Release on the IAPWS Industrial Formulation 1997 for the Thermodynamic Properties of Water and Steam (International Association for the Properties of Water and Steam, Lucerne, 2007; editorial update 2012). The formulation behind the ASME steam tables since 1997.
saturated-steam-properties.freeAccess: Free at iapws.org/technical-guidance/release/IF97-Rev. The coefficients are its Tables 2, 10, 11 and 34. Its computer-program verification values (Tables 5, 15, 35 and 36: 18 values of volume, enthalpy, saturation pressure and saturation temperature) are reproduced to 9 significant digits by this implementation, and a unit test holds them.
saturated-steam-properties.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
saturated-steam-properties.editionNote: Enthalpy is measured from liquid water at the triple point (32.018 F), the convention of US steam tables, so values line up with a printed table. Latent heat falls and saturation temperature rises with pressure. Gauge pressure depends on the local atmosphere: at 5,000 ft (about 12.2 psia) the same gauge reading is a lower absolute pressure and a lower boiling point. Saturated conditions only; region 1 and region 2 of the formulation meet the saturation line up to 623.15 K (2,397 psia), and this tile stops at 2,300 psia.

assumptions.name: Saturated
assumptions.value: dry saturated steam and saturated water; no superheat, wetness or subcooling

assumptions.name: Atmosphere
assumptions.value: 14.696 psia unless entered; valid 8 to 16 psia

assumptions.name: Range
assumptions.value: 0.1 to 2,300 psia absolute

assumptions.name: Unit conversions
assumptions.value: exact definitions of the pound, foot and International Table Btu

contact-time-baffling.formula: TDT = volume at the minimum operating level / peak hourly flow (min); T (t10) = TDT x BF (EPA Eq. 4-3); BF = 0.1 unbaffled, 0.3 poor, 0.5 average, 0.7 superior, 1.0 plug flow (EPA Table 4-2), or an entered tracer-study factor; CT = outlet residual x T.
contact-time-baffling.edition: EPA 815-R-20-003, Disinfection Profiling and Benchmarking Technical Guidance Manual (June 2020), Section 4.4, Equation 4-3, Table 4-2, and Example 4-1, read at epa.gov on 2026-09-30. The primacy agency's tracer-study or baffling-factor determination governs.
contact-time-baffling.freeAccess: A free EPA guidance manual; the five published baffling factors are restated as selectable values and the arithmetic is volume over flow.
contact-time-baffling.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
contact-time-baffling.editionNote: Contact time is the time by which only 10% of the water has passed through, and an unbaffled vessel reaches it at a tenth of its detention time because the inflow short-circuits to the outlet. Temporary systems built from pillow bladders, frac tanks, and totes with one inlet and one outlet are unbaffled or poorly baffled, so volume over pump rate overstates their contact time three to ten times; a pipeline is close to plug flow and earns 1.0. The minimum operating level and the peak hourly flow are the conservative case the guidance requires. Example 4-1 (40 ft diameter, 30 ft minimum depth, 347 gpm, unbaffled) prints 282,000 gal, 813 minutes, and 81.3 minutes with pi = 3.14 and 7.48 gal per cubic foot; the exact constants give 282,009 gal and 81.27 minutes.

assumptions.name: Minimum operating level
assumptions.value: the volume when the tank is drawn down, not the nominal capacity

assumptions.name: Peak hourly flow
assumptions.value: the flow when the least water is in the tank and the most is leaving

assumptions.name: A tracer study supersedes the factor
assumptions.value: the Table 4-2 factors are judgments of the hydraulics, and the primacy agency may require a study or assign a factor

flood-uplift-cover-slab.formula: uplift pressure p = gamma_w x h (62.4 pcf fresh, 64.0 salt); force = p x area (round cover pi/4 D^2); slab resistance = 150 pcf x thickness = 12.5 psf per inch; net = p - resistance; floating head = resistance / gamma_w; counterweight = force - own weight when positive.
flood-uplift-cover-slab.edition: FEMA P-55, Coastal Construction Manual, Volume II, Eq. 8.4 (vertical hydrostatic force), and USACE St. Paul District, Flood Fight Handbook (2016), Section 5.7 (manhole covers under head). The engineer of record and the utility govern.
flood-uplift-cover-slab.freeAccess: FEMA P-55 and the USACE Flood Fight Handbook are free federal publications.
flood-uplift-cover-slab.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
flood-uplift-cover-slab.editionNote: Uplift is the vertical half of hydrostatics and is easy to forget. A slab resists only with its weight plus whatever holds it down, so a 4 in slab lifts under 0.8 ft of head, and a basement pumped dry while the ground outside is saturated can have several feet beneath it -- why floors heave after floods and why basements are pumped down in stages. A manhole cover under a surcharged sewer takes about a ton at 10 ft of head, which sandbags stacked on it will not hold; the handbook's advice is to ring the manhole to reduce the head, or pump it. The handbook prints 2,060 lb for that case, which implies about 65.6 pcf; the tile reports 1,960 lb at 62.4 pcf.

assumptions.name: Water unit weight
assumptions.value: 62.4 pcf fresh, 64.0 pcf salt

assumptions.name: Slab weight
assumptions.value: normal-weight concrete at 150 pcf, 12.5 psf per inch

assumptions.name: Hold-down
assumptions.value: own weight only; no reinforcement, wall connection, soil cover, or relief drainage
